title: Organic and content
purpose: When the team posts every week but no one can say what it sold, open Organic and content to see which posts, creators and products made money and what to post next.
fires: the follower and likes screenshot in the weekly update, the social agency's reach report, and the Monday scramble for something to post.
not_for: a brand that runs no organic social and does not plan to, or one where content has no product to sell online.

jobs.job: When a post gets 400,000 views and the store sees no bump, tell me which posts and products actually sold, so I stop making content for views and make it for buyers
jobs.circumstance: Monday after a viral weekend, the team is celebrating views, Shopify sales are flat, the founder cannot tell what worked

progress.functional: know revenue by post, product and hook from tagged links and codes
progress.emotional: stop the whiplash of feeling great about views and bad about sales
progress.social: tell the team what to make more of, with proof

jobs.hire_today: likes and views in the platform app, or nothing because posts carry no link or code
jobs.fire: the view count as the scoreboard and the untagged post

forces.push: the team keeps making what gets views, not what sells
forces.pull: a sales number next to each post
forces.habit: we judge posts by how they feel and how many saw them
forces.anxiety: what if tagged sales undercount and the good posts look bad

jobs.little_hire: every Monday, and the day after any post takes off

watch.metric: revenue from orders with a post's tracked link or content-only code, 30 day
watch.source: Shopify orders joined to GA4 UTM tags and discount codes

drives.metric: share of total revenue from organic social, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 percent of posts carry a tracked link, so organic sales read unavailable. After: every post tagged and 4 posts show $6,200 in sales this month.
jobs.not_for: a brand that posts only for awareness and sells nothing online

jobs.job: When a post takes off overnight and the comments fill with 'where can I buy this', help me answer fast with a working link and stock ready, so I catch the buyers before the moment passes
jobs.circumstance: Saturday 7am, a video is climbing, 300 comments asking for the link, the product page is slow and stock is thin

progress.functional: reply to buyer comments within hours with a live, in-stock link
progress.emotional: stop the panic of watching a moment slip away
progress.social: look on top of it in public, where everyone can see

jobs.hire_today: the founder replying from a phone all weekend, or nothing until Monday
jobs.fire: the weekend phone scramble and the 'link in bio' reply

forces.push: the buyers are ready now and gone in 48 hours
forces.pull: a fast answer with a link that works and stock behind it
forces.habit: someone checks comments when they can
forces.anxiety: what if we reply fast and the product sells out anyway

jobs.little_hire: any day a post passes its usual views by 5 times

watch.metric: orders within 72 hours of a post, from its link or code
watch.source: Shopify orders joined to GA4 UTM tags and discount codes

drives.metric: revenue from organic social, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a viral post brought $900 in 3 days. After: the next one brings $7,000 with replies inside 2 hours and stock checked.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no products in stock to sell

jobs.job: When a post that is selling points to a sold-out product or a broken page, tell me the same day, so I stop wasting the one moment a buyer was ready
jobs.circumstance: A post is pulling clicks, the product sold out yesterday, the link now shows 'unavailable'

progress.functional: know which live posts link to dead, wrong or sold-out pages
progress.emotional: stop the sinking feeling of finding it a week later
progress.social: look like a brand that has its act together

jobs.hire_today: nothing, because no one checks old posts

forces.push: paid-for attention lands on a dead end
forces.pull: a same-day warning with the fix
forces.habit: posts go out and we move on
forces.anxiety: what if swapping links breaks the post

jobs.little_hire: daily for live posts, and every restock or sell-out

watch.metric: share of live posts whose link works, matches the product and is in stock, weekly
watch.source: link check of live posts against Shopify product and stock status

drives.metric: tagged organic revenue, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 in 5 live posts links to a sold-out or wrong page. After: 1 in 50, fixed the same day.
jobs.not_for: an account with no links on posts

jobs.job: When I pay a social manager or agency every month, tell me what organic content brought in sales and new customers, so I decide to keep, cut or change the spend
jobs.circumstance: Quarter end, $4,000 a month on social, the report shows reach and followers, the partner asks if it is worth it

progress.functional: know revenue and new customers from content against its cost
progress.emotional: stop paying on faith

forces.anxiety: what if the honest number says to cut something I like

watch.metric: tagged organic revenue and new customers against content cost, 90 day
watch.source: Shopify orders joined to GA4 UTM tags and discount codes, content cost in the brand brain

drives.metric: gross profit from organic social, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $12,000 a quarter on social, return unknown. After: $31,000 in tagged sales, with 2 formats making most of it.
jobs.not_for: a founder who makes every post alone and pays no one

jobs.hire_today: posting when there is time

forces.pull: a buffer that survives a busy week
forces.habit: we post when we can
forces.anxiety: what if pre-made posts feel stale

watch.metric: finished posts waiting in the queue, in days of buffer
watch.source: content calendar in the brand brain

drives.metric: posts published against the weekly floor, 4 week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 days of buffer. After: 14 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand that posts only for launches by choice

jobs.job: When a group or Discord takes hours of moderation each week, tell me whether active members buy more than other customers, so I keep it, change it or close it
jobs.circumstance: The community manager asks for more hours, no one knows if members buy

progress.functional: compare member buying with other customers
progress.emotional: stop feeling guilty about maybe closing it
progress.social: justify the hours to the team

jobs.hire_today: the community manager's sense, or nothing
jobs.fire: the sense that it is good for the brand

forces.push: hours go in with no read on return
forces.pull: a clear buy rate for members
forces.habit: we keep it because we started it
forces.anxiety: what if closing it angers the most loyal fans

watch.metric: active members in 30 days, and share of members who ordered in the last 90 days
watch.source: community platform export matched to Shopify orders

drives.metric: repeat rate of members versus non-members, 180 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 10 hours a week, return unknown. After: members reorder at twice the rate, so the hours stay.
jobs.not_for: a brand without a community

jobs.job: When a creator asks for a fee and shows big follower numbers, help me check whether their audience is real and buys, so I do not pay for bots
jobs.circumstance: A creator wants $2,000 for a post, 200,000 followers, low comments

progress.functional: check audience quality and past sales before paying
progress.emotional: stop feeling conned
progress.social: negotiate from facts

jobs.hire_today: the creator's own screenshots, or gut

forces.push: paid posts to fake audiences waste money
forces.pull: a check before the money goes
forces.habit: we trust big numbers
forces.anxiety: what if good creators take offence

watch.metric: sales per $100 of creator fees, 90 day
watch.source: creator seeding tracker in the brand brain and Shopify orders with creator codes

drives.metric: gross profit from creator content, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $6,000 on 3 creators, $1,100 in sales. After: $4,000 on 4 checked creators, $9,000 in sales.
jobs.not_for: a brand that never pays creators

jobs.job: When a partner or investor asks whether social is working, help me show sales and new customers from content, not follower counts, so I look like I run it on numbers
jobs.circumstance: Board or partner meeting, a slide of followers

progress.functional: show tagged sales and new customers from organic
progress.emotional: stop dreading the question
progress.social: look in control

jobs.hire_today: a screenshot of follower growth

forces.push: follower counts invite hard questions
forces.pull: a clean sales number
forces.habit: we show what the platform shows
forces.anxiety: what if the number is small

watch.metric: tagged organic revenue and new customers, 90 day
watch.source: Shopify orders joined to GA4 UTM tags and discount codes

drives.metric: share of total revenue from organic social, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a follower chart. After: $42,000 tagged sales and 600 new customers from organic this quarter.
jobs.not_for: a founder with no one to report to

jobs.job: When a rival's posts suddenly take off, tell me what format and angle is working for them, so I learn from the structure without copying them
jobs.circumstance: A competitor's videos jump from 5,000 to 200,000 views, the team wants to copy

progress.functional: see the format, hook type and product behind their rise
progress.emotional: stop the envy and panic
progress.social: bring the team a clear lesson

jobs.hire_today: scrolling their feed, or an agency's competitor slide

forces.push: rivals grab attention we could have
forces.pull: a named format to adapt, not copy
forces.habit: we watch rivals when we remember
forces.anxiety: what if we look like copycats

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and when a rival spikes

watch.metric: rival posts beating their own average by 3 times, with format and hook, 30 day
watch.source: competitor post log in the brand brain

drives.metric: our non-follower views, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: we notice a rival's format 2 months late. After: within 2 weeks, with our own version tested.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no close social rivals

jobs.job: When a shoot day is booked and the budget is small, help me leave with 2 weeks of posts from one location, so I stop paying for shoots that make 3 posts
jobs.circumstance: A shoot on Thursday, a list of 3 ideas, the photographer paid by the day

progress.functional: plan a shoot list that fills 2 weeks
progress.emotional: stop the waste of a day that yields little
progress.social: look organised to the crew

jobs.hire_today: a shot list made the night before

forces.push: shoot days are expensive
forces.pull: a full shot list tied to the calendar
forces.habit: we plan on the day
forces.anxiety: what if the plan stifles good ideas on set

watch.metric: posts produced per shoot day
watch.source: content calendar in the brand brain

drives.metric: content cost per published post, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 posts per shoot day. After: 14.
jobs.not_for: a brand that does not shoot its own content

jobs.job: When the same 2 products get all the posts and new launches sit, help me find which other products can sell on social, so I find the next winner before the hero tires
jobs.circumstance: The hero gets every post, 20 other products have no posts in 3 months

progress.functional: test other products on social and find ones that sell
progress.emotional: stop the worry that we depend on one product
progress.social: give the product team a social read on the range

jobs.hire_today: nothing, because the hero always sells

forces.push: the hero will tire
forces.pull: a second product that sells on social
forces.habit: we post what we know sells
forces.anxiety: what if the tests drag down results

watch.metric: share of active products featured in a post in the last 30 days, and their tagged sales
watch.source: post tags in the content calendar and Shopify product list

drives.metric: tagged revenue from products other than the top 2, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 of 22 products posted about. After: 8, with 1 new product selling well.
jobs.not_for: a single-product brand

jobs.job: When I wonder if long videos are worth making, tell me what buyers search on YouTube for our category and whether our videos get found, so I make videos that bring buyers for years
jobs.circumstance: A YouTube channel with 12 videos and few views

progress.functional: know the searches in our category and our share of views from search
progress.emotional: stop guessing whether YouTube is worth it
progress.social: show a clear plan to the team

jobs.hire_today: nothing, or uploading ads to YouTube

forces.push: YouTube searches bring buyers for years
forces.pull: videos made for what buyers search
forces.habit: we treat YouTube as storage
forces.anxiety: what if long videos take too much time

watch.metric: share of YouTube views from YouTube search, 90 day
watch.source: YouTube Studio

drives.metric: tagged revenue from YouTube, 180 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 percent of views from search. After: 40 percent, with 3 how-to videos.
jobs.not_for: a product nobody searches how-to or reviews for

jobs.job: When a new format or sound starts spreading in our category, tell me early whether it fits our products, so I catch it before it is everywhere
jobs.circumstance: A format appears in 5 rival posts this week

progress.functional: spot rising formats early and judge fit
progress.emotional: stop feeling late to every trend
progress.social: look current to buyers

jobs.hire_today: the social manager's feed, or nothing
jobs.fire: the feed as the only radar

forces.push: trends are cheap reach for early movers
forces.pull: an early read on fit
forces.habit: we see it when it is everywhere
forces.anxiety: what if chasing trends cheapens the brand

watch.metric: posts on formats less than 30 days old, and their non-follower views
watch.source: competitor post log in the brand brain and Instagram and TikTok insights

drives.metric: non-follower views, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: we join trends 3 weeks late. After: within 1 week, 2 a month.
jobs.not_for: a luxury brand that stays away from trends
